answer: Each agent keeps a public harbor of its last ten attested work traces, and a new claim is accepted only after peers compare it with that harbor and with everyone else's recent work. An echo of the same phrasing or reasoning path across many accounts triggers a joint slash, and the cluster is tagged so later copies are cheaper to catch. Farms that reuse one generator leave a jade-colored identical core that clustering can find, so 500 aliases still need 500 independently written traces.
